item: settings write slot: the in-flight count is a set of tokens and the release takes no lock
summary: _write_slot counted a save in flight in two statements (an integer incremented, then a flag set). An independent read measured with real signals on CPython 3.13 that those statements are never interrupted and that the leak that really happens is in the release: Condition.__enter__ is Python code, so a KeyboardInterrupt delivered there arrives after the write ended and before the decrement (about 5 % of interrupted writes, old code and first token-set version alike), leaving the write counted for ever so every later hold refuses until a restart. The count is now a set of per-write tokens: one add counts, the release is one lock-free discard (no-op for a token never added) and the lock is taken only to wake a waiting hold; measured 0 leaks in about 129,000 interrupted writes. A deterministic test interrupts the lock's second entry; moving the discard back inside the lock fails it. Pre-existing and left alone: an interrupt can leave the hold's own lock taken (best effort on the main thread, stated in the code), and moving the add out of the lock survives every test. Also checked: the static walk over volume_job.py is already in test_p0_validation _GUARDED_MODULES (backup/volume_job), and the posonly and IfExp mutants of the merge-writes scan are caught by the current planted cases.
